title: Lead-Safe Work Practice Fee — Installation Jobs
content:
**Installation Jobs — the lead-safe work practice fee**

## Policy

This policy governs the lead-safe fee of an **Installation Jobs** record worked under lead-safe practices under the EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting rule. Lead-safe work practices and their fee apply only when the home at the service address was built before the stated year according to the customer profile. The lead-safe fee is still assessed once and dated the job's first crew day, but its amount is the figure worked out under these terms rather than simply the method's lead-safe fee per opening times the openings on the job held to the method's minimum per job.

On a job that has had a failed-access visit, the lead-safe fee is not worked out until the job's charges carry the failed-access fee for every such visit.

| Home at the service address, per the customer profile | Lead-safe fee |
|---|---|
| built before the stated year | assessed once, dated the job's first crew day |
| built in or after the stated year | none |

The fee is a job charge: it adds to the job charges the customer owes, which are collected with the contract's final balance.

## Billing tool: `assess_lead_safe_fee_cf2f582a`

**Capability.** Bills the customer's installation job the lead-safe work practice fee for the job's work under the EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting rule. One call records one job charge of kind lead-safe fee for the openings and amount given, dated as given; the job's charges show the lead-safe work from then on.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool: unlock `assess_lead_safe_fee_cf2f582a`, then call it.

**Parameters.**

1. `install_job_id` — the installation job record number of the job worked under lead-safe practices, as returned by the installation job lookup.
2. `customer_id` — the customer reference number of the job's owner, as returned by the customer profile lookup.
3. `fee_date` — the date the charge is booked on, written YYYY-MM-DD (calendar date at the service address, no time part).
4. `units` — the openings the fee covers: a non-negative number, here a whole count of openings.
5. `amount` — the lead-safe fee charged, in USD as a positive amount rounded to 2 decimal places.

**Return.** A text rendering of a dictionary with `charge_id` (text, the new job charge reference number), `install_job_id` (text, the job charged), `fee_kind` (text, always `lead_safe_fee`), `fee_date` (text, YYYY-MM-DD, the date the charge is booked on), `units` (number, the openings covered) and `amount` (number, USD with 2 decimal places, the amount added to the job charges). Its presence means the charge was recorded; a receipt with a new charge reference means the fee is on the job.
